question: Should the core package updater officially preserve local packaged `dist` mutations and offer opt-in replay after update?
rationale: The implementation is technically strong, but it creates a durable public update contract and ongoing filesystem-security and release-compatibility ownership that tests cannot authorize.

options.title: Support preservation and replay
options.body: Approve the default recovery bundle plus explicit replay flag, including the transaction and legacy-version policy.

options.title: Preserve without replay
options.body: Keep recovery capture and reporting but remove automatic replay and its CLI flag to narrow the mutation boundary.

options.title: Do not support dist mutations
options.body: Decline the feature and direct customization to source installs or plugin surfaces instead of packaged-code edits.

recommendation.title: Support preservation and replay
recommendation.body: Approve the default recovery bundle plus explicit replay flag, including the transaction and legacy-version policy.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the live assignee and strongest current-history owner across update staging, package validation, and fs-safe adoption.
